title: A complete Rails application on AWS: trace four journeys
outcome: Explain the request, attachment, background job, and event paths, including cost and recovery choices.
useCase: A holistic architecture explanation and cloud design interview/work review.
benefits: Connects services to user journeys and operating decisions.
drawbacks: The full design is a learning reference; a small product should select only justified parts.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: Trace the journey, not the logos.

trace.title: User identity and edge
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Use a modular Rails app with web and workers, PostgreSQL as the business source, private attachments, a cache, and deliberate event delivery.

Choose ECS/Fargate as one baseline; EKS is an alternative when Kubernetes benefits justify it. They are not two layers every app must run together.

Trace four journeys: a user opens a ticket, uploads an attachment, requests a report, and completes a ticket that updates reporting.

For each, name identity, network, authoritative write, asynchronous boundary, user-visible state, and recovery path.

Then stress the design: one zone fails, the provider slows, a worker repeats, the DB pool fills, a secret rotates, or a user loses access.

Cost reasoning includes always-on capacity, storage/retention, data transfer, NAT/endpoints, logs, and managed service overhead. Use current regional pricing when actually provisioning; this course does not promise a free deployment.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
For each journey, point to where success is durable. A report request is not a ready file.

An outbox commit is not a consumed event. A cache hit is not a new permission grant.

Write one runbook for a growing report age and one restore rehearsal for PostgreSQL/object metadata. Define RPO (acceptable data loss window) and RTO (acceptable recovery time) in plain task terms.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
Putting every named tool into one diagram can create needless operational burden. HA without restore/reconciliation evidence is incomplete.

A rollback cannot unsend notifications or restore all deleted data.
